anchor: By contrast, the identically informed reactive controller loses burst3 at every lead and burst4/5 beyond 45 seconds.
claim_text: Reactive controller fails burst3 at all leads and burst4/5 beyond 45s lead.

adjudication.observed: burst4: 904.739 ms (is_violation = false), burst5: 3250.164 ms (is_violation = true) at lead_s = 165
adjudication.evidence: At lead 165 s (beyond 45 s), the current reactive controller run for the encoder pool (a2:burst4_reactive_L165) achieves p99 delay of 904.739 ms, passing the 1000 ms SLA (is_violation = false).
adjudication.fix: Amend the text to state that the reactive controller fails burst5 beyond 45 s (and both at 300 s target-time), but passes burst4 at lead 165 s (904.74 ms) under issue-time actuation.
adjudication.query: SELECT run_id, window_name, lead_s, achieved_p99_ms, is_violation FROM provenance.v_infraction WHERE is_current = true AND policy = 'reactive' AND experiment = 'a2' AND window_name IN ('burst4', 'burst5') AND lead_s = 165 ORDER BY window_name;

adjudication.observed: For burst3, burst4, and burst5 at leads 60, 120, and 300 seconds, each window-lead group has 2/2 violating metric rows (ITL and TTFT); request denominators are 3093, 25639, and 8983 respectively, with raw TTFT backing present.
adjudication.evidence: All current, unsuperseded a11 reactive language-pool rows violate both SLA metrics at every tested lead (60, 120, and 300 seconds), so burst3 fails throughout and burst4/5 fail at all tested leads beyond 45 seconds.
adjudication.query:
WITH backing AS (
  SELECT i.run_id, i.window_name, i.lead_s, i.sla_metric, i.bound_ms,
         i.achieved_p99_ms, i.is_violation, i.n_requests, i.has_raw_backing,
         i.is_current, d.superseded_by
  FROM provenance.v_infraction AS i
  JOIN provenance.v_dim AS d USING (run_id)
  WHERE i.experiment = 'a11'
    AND i.policy = 'reactive'
    AND i.pool = 'language'
    AND i.window_name IN ('burst3', 'burst4', 'burst5')
    AND i.is_current = true
    AND d.is_current = true
    AND d.superseded_by IS NULL
), per_window AS (
  SELECT window_name, lead_s,
         count(*) AS metric_rows,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_violation) AS violating_metric_rows,
         array_agg(sla_metric ORDER BY sla_metric) AS metrics,
         min(n_requests) AS n_requests,
         bool_and(has_raw_backing) FILTER (WHERE sla_metric = 'ttft') AS ttft_has_raw_backing
  FROM backing
  GROUP BY window_name, lead_s
)
SELECT window_name, lead_s, metric_rows, violating_metric_rows, metrics,
       n_requests, ttft_has_raw_backing
FROM per_window
ORDER BY window_name, lead_s
